category_title: Year 9 boys with SEBD who resist modified games and technical practice
scenario_title: Modifying familiar games to teach defensive principles
minimal_context: The student is participating in a physical education soccer lesson where the rules have been modified to focus on defensive principles.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Today we are playing soccer, but to practice the principles of defending, like pressure on the ball and denial of the ball, we are going to play a modified version with restricted zones.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: We all play football as our main sport. We're already familiar with the concepts and don't need to learn too much.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Let's just try it this way for a bit and see how it goes.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Discusses the rules briefly with the group, but upon returning to the field, completely ignores the zones and applies minimal defensive principles)

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Remember to keep trying to use the defensive principles we talked about in your groups.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: This is stupid! I'm not doing this modified stuff anymore. We just want to play the 'real' game!

task.content: principles of defending in games such as pressure on the ball, denial of the ball and helping away from the ball

context.materials: Soccer game, equipment for unfamiliar sports
context.social_setting: Class of Year 9 boys with SEBD, group discussions

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: when Amy changed aspects of the soccer game played to emphasise the principle of defending being taught
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: met by pupil dissention, wanted to play the ‘real’ game rather than one that was modiﬁed by the teacher
challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: they are familiar with the concepts and think they don’t need to learn too much

behavior_patterns.condition: engaging the class in discussion around a particular defensive principle
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: pupils would discuss in groups the questions set but, in returning to play the game, application of the principle was minimal
